Athens: The Fragility of the Republic
The Golden Age: Pericles championed a democracy where
citizens were honored for virtue, not lineage or wealth. A
rare, rational pursuit of justice.
The Decay: True democracy was short-lived. The insatiable
pursuit of material wealth led to class warfare between
democrats and oligarchs.
The Symptom: The execution of Socrates (399 BC). Accused
of impiety and corrupting youth, his death by hemlock was a
targeted assassination by an elite class threatened by his
exposure of their ignorance and greed.

The Myth of European Superiority
The Reality of the "Civilized" West
The Reality of the "Savage" Americas
During the 12th century, Frankish (European) medicine was
remarkably primitive. Arab chronicler Usama in Mungidh
recorded a Frankish doctor treating an abscess with a lethal
axe amputation, and a mental illness by cutting a cross into a
woman's skull to "release the demon," killing her instantly.
Long before European contact, Mesoamerican cities boasted
highly advanced urban sanitation. By 1000 BC, the Olmec
city of San Lorenzo had functional drainage systems,
centuries ahead of the open-sewer squalor of Medieval
Europe.
